event: Quick check for other docs on async register bounds.

I verified the finding: no other spec text answers the question. I searched the `aon_timer` markdown and hjson files for terms like "slow clock", "cycles", "synchron", "read-back", "take effect" and "latency". The only relevant text is `theory_of_operation.md` lines 25–28. Those lines say a write can complete early and that a read-back guarantees all earlier writes have completed. They give no cycle bound. The verdict was accepted.

The one near miss is `dv/README.md` line 36, which only mentions synchronisation logic between the clock domains. It is a verification document and gives no bound either.

For the fix, I recommended that the spec either state a maximum latency in AON and SYS cycles, or say outright that read-back ordering is the only guarantee.
